description:
This starfish eats coral reefs alive, and divers kill it with household vinegar.
The crown-of-thorns starfish grows up to 80 centimetres across with up to 21 arms and hundreds of toxin-tipped spines. It feeds by pushing its stomach out through its mouth over living coral and digesting the tissue, leaving white skeleton behind. One adult can eat about 10 square metres of coral a year, and a female can produce up to 50 million eggs. Outbreaks have been one of the biggest causes of coral loss on the Great Barrier Reef, so divers control them by injecting individual starfish with vinegar or bile salts.
Should we be killing one species to save a reef?
first_comment: Cut one in half and both halves can grow back into a starfish, which is why divers switched to injections. What other animal is almost impossible to get rid of?
